reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it primarily provides chart-based instruction on Bitcoin and Solana, covering support, resistance, trendlines, entries, stop-losses, and take-profit levels with TradingView visuals. Although it discusses a prospective long trade, reward ratios, trading signals, and links to exchanges or communities, these are framed as tutorial or educational content without a guaranteed return, required payment, deception, victim loss, or completed transaction.

opening.argument: Judge, the proposed upside is tied to an action viewers are encouraged to take. The description promises instruction on how to “forecast price targets for profitable long positions,” and the speaker turns that prospect into a near-term direction: “so meaning you will try to go for a long position this week on solani.” He supplies an entry and target, while the description directs viewers to create exchange accounts. Read together, this is more than an abstract chart lesson: it gives viewers a route from an anticipated gain to participation.

so meaning you will try to go for a long position this week on solani
so our target to the long position bring it to the entry around here which is 88 or 90 USD.
Create and verify your Binance account

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited daily-timeframe instruction and stop-loss show that charting is part of the presentation; they do not erase the invitation to take this week's long position. Nor does the absence of a guaranteed return settle whether a projected profitable trade is being used to solicit participation. The speaker's own phrasing moves from analysis to what the viewer should try to do.

citations.quote: so meaning you will try to go for a long position this week on solani

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Those excerpts establish a proposed trade, not a deceptive token-sale offer or promised appreciation. The same presentation specifies a stop-loss, making downside part of the example, and its disclaimer says the material is educational and that viewers trade at their own risk. An exchange-account link does not establish that anyone must register or buy SOL to receive a promised return.

This video is for educational purposes only and does not constitute financial, investment, or trading advice. Trade at your own risk.

opening.argument: Judge, consider the signals together. The speaker says that when Bitcoin rises, “just know solana will also go up,” says the week's trade will be long, and points to a prior trade that “went to take profit.” Against those confidence-building claims, the description places exchange referral and verification links in the viewer's path. Each detail can be explained individually, but their combination can make a speculative SOL trade feel validated and immediately actionable.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense identifies legitimate chart tools, but tools alone do not establish that the confidence attached to the forecast is warranted. Its cited stop-loss acknowledges downside without substantiating the claim that SOL will follow Bitcoin upward. The relevant concern is the cumulative effect of that certainty, a successful-trade anecdote, and a route to an exchange.

citations.quote: if bitcoin is going up, just know solana will also go up.
so this was a trade i took some few weeks ago when i was in china which went to take profit

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A confident forecast and a past-trade anecdote do not show a fabricated result or guaranteed future profit. The speaker also describes SOL as potentially falling, supplies a stop-loss, and tells viewers to understand a token before buying it. Those qualifications fit speculative market commentary, even if its forecast is too confident.

opening.argument: Judge, the tutorial also functions as a pathway toward trading. After describing TradingView analysis, the speaker asks viewers to consider a SOL long position and says to select the exchange “where your money is.” The description offers exchange-account links, while the speaker points viewers toward his community and says he sometimes shares trading signals. The chart instruction may be genuine, but it also builds trust before directing attention to a specific trade and places where viewers can act on it.

citations.quote: so meaning you will try to go for a long position this week on solani
going to select where your money is so if you are trading on binance you select binance
Create and verify your Binance account
And sometimes I also share my trading signal.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense calls the links and community incidental to education, yet the speaker connects his chart exercise to a position viewers should try this week. Teaching support, resistance, and stop-loss placement does not make that invitation disappear. The question is whether the instructional format also promotes participation; the cited call to take a long position supports that reading.

citations.quote: so meaning you will try to go for a long position this week on solani

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotion and instruction can coexist without establishing a scam. The speaker walks through support, resistance, and a possible stop-loss; the exchange selection is explicitly conditional on where someone already trades. Neither the links nor occasional signals demonstrate a required purchase, a false promise, or a completed loss.
